name: template-build-checks
body: Template registry build checks: when the project's templates are loaded (startup and reload), the registry enforces the template-set integrity laws (requirements.constraint.template-registry-integrity) and reports each violation as a templates error path-qualified to the offending `template.yaml`/`example.md` (templates-dir-validation step 4). The enforced laws are: every reference chain is acyclic — a cycle is rejected with the chain in the error, e.g. `sections/a → sections/b → sections/a` (requirements.constraint.section-cycle-error-chain); no composition chain exceeds six heading levels (`#`…`######`, requirements.constraint.section-depth-limit); a section declaration accepts only templates under `templates/sections/` (directory-kind check); a field type is a section template (never a slide template and never a required-body template); a template name is unique across `templates/slides/` and `templates/sections/` (cross-kind name uniqueness); declared field/section names avoid the reserved `deck`/`slide`/`item`/`raw`/`data`/`notes`/`body` names and the reserved `_format` suffix (requirements.constraint.reserved-template-names); every referenced template is defined; the `section` helper's calls are reference edges too — each helper target must be a defined section-usage template, each literal `dict` fields key must be a declared field of the target, the target's required fields must be present or defaulted, a target declaring a child section of min>0 is rejected, and helper calls participate in cycle rejection (section-helper-load-checks); and each `example.md` — including a container template's example with nested instances — validates against its template recursively (nested-section-validation). These are templates errors, distinct from deck (slide) errors.
